headline: PAGASA Raises Red Rainfall Warning in Zambales, Bataan and Pampanga
seoTitle: PAGASA Raises Red Rainfall Warning in Central Luzon | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA placed Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga and parts of Tarlac and Bulacan under a red rainfall warning early August 30 as Habagat rains continued.
deck: The 5 a.m. warning indicated serious flooding risk in flood-prone areas as prolonged Habagat rain continued across western and central Luzon.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA placed Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga and specified parts of Tarlac and Bulacan under a red rainfall warning at 5 a.m. on Sunday, August 30, as the Southwest Monsoon continued to bring heavy rain.
A red warning indicates serious flooding in flood-prone areas. Other parts of Central and Southern Luzon, including Metro Manila, were under orange or yellow warnings at that issuance.

sections.heading: Heavy-rain outlook
paragraphs: PAGASA's outlook projected 100 to 200 millimeters of rain from Saturday to Sunday noon over Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac and Pampanga.
The bureau said rainfall could be higher in mountainous areas and that impacts could be worsened by significant rain already received.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: This update keeps the developing Habagat event on FMB News' established canonical route and removes a separate August 30 weather route created from the same sequence.
Rainfall-warning boundaries can change within hours. The 5 a.m. locations are a timestamped record, not a substitute for the latest PAGASA advisory.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated rain can quickly worsen flooding and slope instability. Communities near rivers, drainage channels and steep terrain should follow evacuation, road-closure and safety instructions from local disaster authorities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should follow the latest PAGASA rainfall warnings and local disaster advisories because warning levels and covered locations may change at the next issuance.
